title: Drop NODE_TRANSFORM_TYPES_FLAG from both launchers now that the daemon graph is erasable, and correct the runbook's manual-wrapper recipe
description:
Follow-up filed by governor-cc0cc843 under ruling msg-541e4475 (2026-09-18) on task-4444d180 step 5, option (B). 4444d180 removed the only non-erasable production syntax (agent-spawn-contract.ts:79) and added `erasableSyntaxOnly` to apps/daemon/tsconfig.json. worker-e0435164 measured that it fires TS1294 on daemon src AND on package sources in the daemon program. It deliberately KEPT `--experimental-transform-types` (NODE_TRANSFORM_TYPES_FLAG) on the launchers with a stated reason: one argv shape shared by `moe up` and `moe start`, where dropping it from one launcher forks them.

UNNAMED CONSUMERS worker-e0435164 found (measured at 4444d180's tree; re-measure before planning):
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-spawn.ts:58 declares the constant only.
- apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts:244 (daemon child) and :366 (wrapper child) compose the argv. moe-up-main.test.ts:281/:354 pin the flag positionally, and after 4444d180 the tripwire arm (formerly :924-927) asserts that plain strip-only node LOADS the wrapper entry.
- apps/daemon/src/projects/project-stack-host-main.ts:17/:74 imports the constant for the `moe start` wrapper argv, and project-stack-host-main.test.ts:208 pins the literal.
- docs/agent-stack-runbook.md:657-676 says the manual wrapper recipe is broken without the flag. That is FALSE after 4444d180, and operators read it.
- packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts has its own TRANSFORM_TYPES literal for the stack entry. Census it and decide it in the same row.

RISK: this changes the argv of the launcher the owner's LIVE projects run through (`moe start`). Before dropping the flag, prove every entry the launchers start (daemon, wrapper, project-stack-host) loads under plain strip-only node at the delivered tree, including any module outside the daemon tsconfig program that the guard does not cover.
definitionOfDone: Every launcher child (moe up daemon + wrapper, moe start project-stack-host + its wrapper, and the Windows stack-boundary entry if it carries its own literal) starts under plain `node` with NO --experimental-transform-types, proven by a real-spawn arm per entry, quoted, at the delivered tree.

NODE_TRANSFORM_TYPES_FLAG and every positional pin of it are removed or re-aimed to assert the flag's ABSENCE by value. No arm deleted or matcher widened to go green. The two-sided strip-only proof from task-4444d180 still holds.
docs/agent-stack-runbook.md's manual-wrapper recipe (~:657-676) states the measured truth, with no claim that the recipe needs the flag.
`pnpm typecheck`, the daemon suite and `pnpm test:e2e` green with count lines quoted. Reds attributed by the path-attributed baseline rule.

implementationPlan.description: RED FIRST — write the committed plain-node spawn arms that will replace the flag as the safety net, before removing anything. These are permanent test arms, not one-off probes: they are the only guard over packages/runner, which `erasableSyntaxOnly` does not cover. For EACH launcher entry, add an arm that spawns `process.execPath` with NO flags against the real entry and asserts it loads, reading by EXIT CODE and the ABSENCE of the error CODE `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX`: the wrapper entry and the daemon entry in apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.test.ts (the wrapper arm may already exist as task-4444d180's inverted tripwire — extend rather than duplicate it), and the project-stack-host entry in apps/daemon/src/projects/project-stack-host-main.test.ts. Then add the NEGATIVE CONTROL that keeps those arms from going vacuously green: spawn plain node with `--input-type=module-typescript -e` over a probe containing a parameter property, and assert it is REFUSED with ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX AND a nonzero exit code. THE TRAP, measured at planning: when Node refuses it ECHOES THE OFFENDING SOURCE LINE into its error output, so any sentinel string you put in the probe source appears in stderr even though the code never ran. NEVER assert the absence of a sentinel from the probe source — it fails on a correctly-refusing run. Assert the error code and the exit code. This negative control replaces the old 'loads with the flag' side of task-4444d180's two-sided proof (DoD 2), which tests nothing the product does once the flag is gone. Run these arms now: the positive arms should already be GREEN (the graph is erasable), and the negative control GREEN — quote both. They exist to STAY green through step 3 and to red on any future regression.

implementationPlan.description: Drop the flag from ALL THREE launchers in this one step, because dropping it from any subset forks the argv shape `moe up` and `moe start` share — which is exactly why task-4444d180 kept it. (1) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.ts: remove NODE_TRANSFORM_TYPES_FLAG from the daemon child argv (:244) and the wrapper child argv (:366) and from the import (:9). (2) apps/daemon/src/projects/project-stack-host-main.ts: remove it from the `moe start` wrapper argv (:74) and the import (:17). (3) packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.ts: remove the local `TRANSFORM_TYPES` literal (:96) and its use in the stack-entry argv (:174). (4) apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-spawn.ts: delete the exported constant (:53) and REPLACE its comment block with a short statement of the measured truth — that every launcher child now loads under plain strip-only node, that the committed spawn arms from step 2 are the guard (covering packages/runner too, which the daemon's `erasableSyntaxOnly` does not), and where those arms live. Deleting an exported symbol: confirm by `git grep -n NODE_TRANSFORM_TYPES_FLAG` that after this step the ONLY remaining references are inside the two test files step 4 re-aims — if anything else still imports it, stop and report. DO NOT TOUCH apps/daemon/src/projects/project-review-drain-native.ts:71: that embedded C# verifies ANOTHER process's identity from its command line and accepts argv WITH or WITHOUT the flag (`script=argv[1]==flag?2:1`). Processes launched by an older packaged artifact still carry the flag, so tightening it to require absence would fail identity verification mid-upgrade. Its tolerance is correct.

Re-aim every positional pin to assert the flag's ABSENCE BY VALUE (DoD 2), never by deletion and never by widening a matcher. apps/daemon/src/orchestrator/moe-up-main.test.ts :281 and :354 asserted `argv[0]` IS the flag; they must now assert the COMPLETE launch argv by value, so a future flag slipped back in at position 0 reds rather than shifting the entry path along unnoticed — asserting only `argv[0] !== flag` would pass for an argv that grew a different flag. :938, the with-flag side of task-4444d180's two-sided proof, is superseded by step 2's negative control; re-aim or replace it so the two-sided proof still holds, and do not simply delete it. apps/daemon/src/projects/project-stack-host-main.test.ts :208 pins the literal inside the `moe start` wrapper argv; re-aim it to assert the full argv by value without the flag. packages/runner/src/platform/windows/windows-project-stack-boundary.test.ts currently pins ONLY `argv: []` (:163, :188, :216) and has NO assertion on the :174 success argv at all — so ADD one there, asserting the decoded launch payload's full argv by value (`[entryPath, --config=…, --asset-root=…]`). That is a new arm, not a re-aim, and it matters: without it the Windows launcher could regrow the flag with nothing to catch it. Then confirm `git grep -n NODE_TRANSFORM_TYPES_FLAG` returns ZERO lines anywhere outside dist/ and .moe/.

Correct the runbook (DoD 3). docs/agent-stack-runbook.md:657-676 currently tells operators the flag is 'currently load-bearing', quotes the ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX failure at `agent-spawn-contract.ts:53`, and says in bold that the manual wrapper recipe 'is broken as written — add --experimental-transform-types to it'. All of that is false after task-4444d180, and operators follow it. Replace the passage with the MEASURED TRUTH, in the same plain register as the surrounding text: the launcher runs its children under plain `node`; the manual three-terminal recipe works as written, wrapper included, with no extra flag; and a plain-node spawn test guards every launcher entry so a construct Node cannot strip is caught before it reaches an operator. Quote the step-1 probe results rather than asserting them. Do not leave a historical 'this used to be broken' paragraph behind — a runbook is read for what to do now, and a stale warning is exactly the defect being fixed. Keep the sentence that follows the passage ('Apart from that, the manual three-terminal recipe is what to reach for when you need a fixed port…') reading naturally after your edit. Leave docs/plans/2026-09-06-repository-delivery-remediation.md alone: it is a historical plan that accurately describes the state at the time it was written.

(B) `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` with its `Test Files N passed` line quoted — read the OUTPUT, not the exit code; a leg with no count line ran nothing.
